title: Anufo language
description: Tano language spoken in West Africa
extract: Anufo (Anufɔ), also known as Chakosi, is an Akan language spoken in northeast Ghana, northern Togo, northwest Benin and Ivory Coast by approximately 180,000 people. Anufɔ is tonal and follows a subject-verb-object canonical structure. Anufɔ is spoken with dialectical differences across nine tribes, though all are mutually intelligible.
